

**DIY Bluetooth-Controlled LED using Arduino and MIT App Inventor**

 **Aim**

To control an LED wirelessly using a mobile phone.

To learn Bluetooth communication between Arduino and a mobile application.

**Components Required**

Arduino board

Bluetooth module (HC-05/HC-06)

LED

220Ω resistor

Breadboard

Jumper wires

USB cable

Android mobile phone

Laptop/PC

**Software Required**

Arduino IDE

MIT App Inventor

Web browser

**Working Principle**

Arduino is connected to the Bluetooth module.

The MIT App Inventor app sends ON/OFF commands from the mobile phone.

Bluetooth receives the command and sends it to Arduino.

Arduino processes the command.

Based on the command, the LED turns ON or OFF.

**Circuit Connections**

LED → Arduino digital pin

LED → 220Ω resistor → GND

Bluetooth module → Arduino serial communication pins

VCC → 5V

GND → GND

**MIT App Inventor**

Create a simple mobile app.

Add Bluetooth connection option.

Add ON and OFF buttons.

ON button sends an ON command.

OFF button sends an OFF command.

**Procedure**

1\. Connect the LED and Bluetooth module to Arduino.

2\. Upload the Arduino program.

3\. Create the control app using MIT App Inventor.

4\. Pair the phone with the Bluetooth module.

5\. Connect the app to the Bluetooth module.

6\. Press ON to turn the LED ON.

7\. Press OFF to turn the LED OFF.

**Applications**

Wireless light control

Home automation

Smart devices

Remote control systems

IoT-based projects

**Conclusion**

This project demonstrates how Arduino, Bluetooth communication, and MIT App Inventor can be combined to create a simple wireless LED control system.

**Result**

The LED was successfully controlled wirelessly using an Android mobile application through Bluetooth and Arduino.
